newsitem.title: GERMANY: German crude oil tenders to start August 4.
newsitem.headline: German crude oil tenders to start August 4.

text.p: Germany plans to hold tenders to sell off strategic crude oil reserves starting in early August, raising around 400 million marks this year, a spokeswoman for the Economics Ministry said on Monday.
The spokeswoman told reporters that the tenders would start from August 4.
Germany was to issue a statement later on Monday providing more details of its planned sale of crude oil reserves, the spokeswoman said.
A government source said earlier this would include the first amount to be sold, the quality and type of oil.
An official of Germany's oil stocks agency also said earlier that this first tender would be of some 450,000 cubic metres, or around 2.8 million barrels, of oil.

There will be up to six tenders as Germany unloads nearly two million tonnes of oil between August and the end of 1997, which is aimed at helping Bonn lower its budget deficit to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
